prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is an enabling method in the sense I weigh most: a whole community of chemists can now make aryl amines routinely, predictably and at scale, in discovery, process and materials chemistry. The advance came from ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and carbenes) and from mechanistic work on oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination, so it rests on a stable and well-supported picture of how the catalyst works. Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalyst systems independently and in parallel, which gives a clean two-person attribution. After more than twenty-five years of independent confirmation there is no maturity risk, and the recognition is overdue.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling, and some members may see C-N coupling as a heteroatom extension of that work rather than a new concept. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precedent that has to be handled in the citation or the discussion. Against the biology-linked candidates, this is also a less dramatic story to tell the public, and a method prize is judged only by what it has enabled, which is easy to take for granted.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B002 first with Buchwald and Hartwig, noting that Kosugi's tin-amide precedent was earlier but used stoichiometric tin, so a two-person prize is cleanest, while the 2010 cross-coupling prize might be seen as covering related ground.
responses.response: I agree on the attribution and share his view that the Kosugi issue is a footnote rather than a blocker. I would go further on the 2010 objection. That prize recognised C-C bond formation with organometallic partners. C-N coupling needed its own ligand-design solution and its own mechanistic understanding (amine binding, deprotonation, beta-hydride elimination as the competing pathway). It is a distinct achievement and was not made redundant by the earlier award.

responses.point: Chabes puts base editing (B029) first as a chemically precise, mechanistically transparent, widely reproduced tool that has already reached clinical use, with Liu as the driver and Komor and Gaudelli as lead experimentalists.
responses.response: I accept that base editing is a clean idea and that Liu's role is clear. My reservations are about attribution and timing. The prize would be given to a trainee-led pair beside the PI while Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID work is a parallel claim, and the 2020 CRISPR prize makes a close follow-up awkward. Long-term clinical outcomes are not yet in. By comparison, C-N coupling has a stable record and a clearly defined group of originators. I do not think opening support for B029 should be taken to mean it is the better-settled case.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B016) first as a molecular design principle (pH-dependent charge for encapsulation and endosomal escape) that made siRNA and mRNA medicines deliverable, with Cullis, Hope and Madden as the core.
responses.response: I agree the impact is enormous and that the pKa design principle is real chemistry. My concern is that the credit is diffuse, as Aili himself notes. Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer each have a plausible claim, and any three-name cut will look arbitrary. The 2023 Medicine prize also partly covered the vaccine consequences. I would want to see a clear argument for who invented the ionizable-lipid concept before I support B016 over a candidate with a clean attribution like B002.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase (B006) first for the structures of the Fe protein, MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor together with kinetic work on the ATP-gated cycle, while acknowledging that three names cannot cover the field and that N2 binding is still debated.
responses.response: Structurally this is the candidate closest to my own interests. The interstitial carbide and the cryo-EM turnover states are real achievements. But I would ask what has actually been determined. The resting-state cofactor is known, the substrate-binding site and the catalytic intermediates are not, so a citation to the mechanism would run ahead of the evidence. A citation limited to the structure of the cofactor would be defensible but would split credit among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Ribbe and Seefeldt. I keep it as my first alternative rather than my preferred choice.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks targeted protein degradation (B018) first as a new pharmacological principle with quantitatively testable chemistry, covering PROTACs and molecular glues through Crews, Deshaies and Handa.
responses.response: I agree that induced proximity is a real new concept and that it is well tested in many labs. I am still concerned that no degrader is approved yet and that the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands came from different groups with different histories. Combining them in a three-person prize works only if the citation can describe both honestly. I would keep B018 as an alternative but it is not yet as settled as B002.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and how the Kosugi precedent should be handled in the citation
Whether a two-person method prize in synthetic catalysis is preferred over a biology-linked topic with stronger public impact
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism will be considered closed enough to support a structure-and-mechanism citation
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: none of the credited candidates for B002, B006 or B018 are my collaborators, mentors or Stockholm University colleagues. My only connection is a general interest in crystallographic methods, which relates most closely to B019 and is not part of my preferred configuration.
